subject: Retaining individual ids when simulating multiple individuals' paths

messages.author: dbb8469ee2e94d03
messages.subject: Retaining individual ids when simulating multiple individuals' paths
parts:
Hi Chris,

I have a telemetry object of multiple individuals. I am using a CTMM fit to one individual to simulate tracks across all individuals, as they all have very similar movement patterns. Is there a way to retain the individual ids from the telemetry object in the simulated tracks? So far the id slot for each simulated track is given the same id, which is the single id from the CTMM object. Here is an abbreviated example:

length(telemdata)
#165 individuals

#fit CTMM model to first individual
mod <- ctmm.select(telemdata[[1]],GUESS)
mod@info$identity
#individual identify of 'mod' CTMM object is "01"

#simulate paths with hourly intervals for each individual in telemdata
sim_paths <- lapply(telemdata, function(x) simulate(mod, data = x, dt=3600, complete = TRUE))

#for all i's
sim_paths[[i]]@info$identity
# = "01"

I'd like each simulated track to be matched with the appropriate id from telemdata/telemetry object rather than from the CTMM object.

Can this be fixed?

Thanks,
Briana

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Retaining individual ids when simulating multiple individuals' paths
parts:
Hi Briana,

I think if the two objects (ctmm & telemetry) have conflicting identities, then I should probably paste them together to not discard the information. I can put that in the next update tomorrow-ish.

If you don't like that, you should be able to do something like

sim_paths <- lapply(telemdata, function(x) { TEL <- simulate(mod, data = x, dt=3600, complete = TRUE) ; TEL@info <- x@info ; return(TEL) } )

to force the identity you want.

Best,
Chris
